_comment: Published downlink budgets, one per satellite (AGENTS.md §13: never invent link parameters).
Every value is quoted from the source or derived from quoted values; derived ones say how in `derivations`.
eirp_dbw is the EIRP where the pattern offset is 0 dB; eirp_pattern holds [off-nadir deg, offset dB] pairs (nadir-pointing), interpolated linearly and held beyond the last point.

station_gt_db_k, system_loss_db and data_rate_bps describe the source's own reference receiving station and budget: system_loss_db sums every loss the budget lists (including implementation/demodulation loss) except the atmospheric/rain loss; data_rate_bps is the rate the source's Eb/N0 is referred to.

atmospheric_loss_db is that loss as the source quotes it at atmospheric_ref_elev_deg; it is scaled along the slant path by the cosecant law. A source that holds it constant at every elevation keeps it in system_loss_db instead.
G/T is the source's value at its worked geometry, held at every elevation (a fraction of a dB conservative away from the horizon).
`checks` are the source's own worked margins; tests/test_linkbudget.py reproduces each to within 0.1 dB.

Excluded while sourcing (2026-10-20): NOAA-15/18/19 (decommissioned 2025); ISS and SO-50 FM voice (analog, no Eb/N0); Metop-B/C AHRPT (TD 18 gives G/T but no EIRP); Meteor-M LRPT, Sentinel-1 X-band and amateur cubesats (no published EIRP / budget found).

profiles.label: X-band HRD 7812 MHz, 15 Mbps QPSK, to a 3 m direct-broadcast dish

sources.title: JPSS-1 Spacecraft HRD to Direct Broadcast Stations RF ICD, 472-00165 Rev A: Table 4-1 and Appendix A, Fig. A-1

derivations.eirp_dbw: Fig. A-1: 7.8 W (38.92 dBm) + 5.5 dBi at 62° off nadir − 2.0 dB passive loss = 42.4 dBm
derivations.eirp_pattern: shape of Table 4-1 minimum EIRP (30.3 / 30.8 / 33.6 / 42.8 dBm at 0 / 17.6 / 42.7 / 61.9° from boresight), relative to its 61.9° value
derivations.system_loss_db: Fig. A-1: polarisation 0.26 + multipath 0.20 + ground pointing 1.00 + implementation 2.50
derivations.atmospheric_loss_db: Fig. A-1: rain & atmospheric 3.65 dB at 5° elevation
derivations.data_rate_bps: 15 Mbps CADU × 223/255 (Reed-Solomon) = 71.18 dB-Hz, as Fig. A-1 uses

profiles.label: X-band HRD 7812 MHz, 25 Mbps OQPSK, to an HRD ground terminal

sources.title: JPSS-2 Spacecraft HRD to DBS RF ICD, 6470-ICD23510 Rev E (472-00340 Rev C): Figs. SC-GND-3318 and SC-GND-4525

derivations.eirp_dbw: Fig. SC-GND-3318: 10.7 W (40.3 dBm) − 0.86 dB transmitter network loss = 39.44 dBm, before antenna gain
derivations.eirp_pattern: antenna gain: the worst case in coverage, −6.6 dBi at 34.2° (Fig. SC-GND-3318), held from nadir to 34.2°; 6.175 dBi at the 62° edge of coverage (Fig. SC-GND-4525 annotation); linear in between
derivations.system_loss_db: Fig. SC-GND-3318: pointing 0.00 (in G/T) + polarisation 1.57 + implementation/multipath 2.70
derivations.atmospheric_loss_db: Fig. SC-GND-3318: excess path loss (incl. scintillation, 99% availability) 0.50 dB at 50.6° elevation; scaled, it gives the required > 1 dB margin at 5° (J2SRD-1589)
derivations.data_rate_bps: 25 Msps CADU (74.0 dB-Hz), the rate Fig. SC-GND-3318 refers Eb/N0 to

profiles.label: X-band MPT 7820 MHz, 45 Mbps QPSK, to a 10 m dish

sources.title: Space-to-Ground Interface Control Document of FY-3D Meteorological Satellite (CMA/NSMC), §5.1.7–5.1.8, Tables 2 and 3 (copy hosted by SatDump)

derivations.eirp_dbw: Table 3: transmitter power 23 W = 13.617 dBW, before antenna gain
derivations.eirp_pattern: Table 2 minimum antenna gain (dBi) by angle off the antenna axis
derivations.system_loss_db: Table 3: atmospheric absorption 0.3 + rain 4.5 (the source holds both constant at every elevation, so they stay here) + pointing 0.5 + polarisation 1.0 + demodulation 1.8
derivations.required_ebn0_db: Table 3: 11.4 dB at BER 1e-7 less the 6.0 dB coding gain of RS(255,223) + CONV(7,3/4)
derivations.data_rate_bps: 60 Msps (77.78 dB), the rate Table 3 refers Eb/N0 to

profiles.label: L-band GRB 1686.6 MHz, 15.5 Mbps per polarisation (DVB-S2), to a G/T 15.2 dB/K user station

sources.title: NOAA OSPO: Link budget for GRB on GOES-R series satellites to user stations, Rev. A (2017-07-25)

derivations.eirp_pattern: 2.0 dB antenna gain reduction at the edge of coverage (17.1 dBi peak, 15.1 dBi EOC), as a parabolic main lobe 2.0·(1 − (θ/8.67°)²); 8.67° is the Earth's edge seen from GEO at 5° elevation
derivations.system_loss_db: pointing 0.5 + cross-polarisation and adjacent-channel interference 2.11 (C/N0 85.0 → 82.89 dB-Hz) + satellite degradations 0.5 + implementation 0.9
derivations.atmospheric_loss_db: all atmospheric losses 2.5 dB at 5° elevation
